question: How can GNN encoders (GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE) be applied end to end to node classification for anti-money laundering and to link prediction for movie recommendation?
contributions: A common graph-processor, encoder, decoder framework (Fig 12.1) applied to two tasks.
PyG code walkthroughs for Elliptic node classification and MovieLens link prediction with a three-encoder comparison.

limits: Single run per model, no seeds or error bars; chapter notes results may differ slightly on rerun.
Random node split on Elliptic, a time-series dataset; no temporal split.
Prose counts differ from the table (Table 12.5 percentages) and GAT licit rates are internally inconsistent.
Hidden width, learning rate, optimizer, batch size for node classification and decision threshold are not stated in the text.
Training loader in Listing 12.21 is built on the full graph (data=data) rather than train_data.
practices: Keep only known-label nodes visible to loss via train/val/test masks (12.1.3).
Use log_softmax with CrossEntropyLoss for node classification (12.1.4).
Split edges with RandomLinkSplit and keep message-passing edges disjoint from supervision edges (12.2.3).
Add reverse edges with ToUndirected so messages flow both ways (12.2.3).
Use LinkNeighborLoader with neighbour sampling for graphs exceeding memory (12.2.3).
Use weighted-average precision/recall/F1 for imbalanced classes (12.1.5).
Use GraphConv rather than GCNConv for heterogeneous graphs (12.2.5 note).
